responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the PDP-11 architecture, covering the machine-dependent part of compilation from RTL expansion through final assembly output. Its main responsibility is to encode the PDP-11 ABI, data layout, register set, condition-code model, floating formats, and assembler conventions, then use that target model to select and emit valid PDP-11 instructions and addressing modes. The core pdp11.h and pdp11.cc/pdp11.c files define static machine properties and executable target hooks for calling conventions, return values, trampolines, register availability, legality and cost decisions, section and symbol emission, and dialect-specific assembler output; pdp11.md provides the RTL machine description for instruction selection, splitting, prologue/epilogue generation, branches, arithmetic, shifts, multiword operations, and floating-point code; constraints.md and predicates.md define the operand classes and matching rules that capture PDP-11-specific registers, immediates, auto-increment/decrement addressing, and CC behavior; pdp11-modes.def adds target-specific condition-code and floating modes; and pdp11.opt records the user-visible target options that control CPU, assembler syntax, integer and floating-point variants, and related backend behavior. Together these files implement the full code-generation policy and assembly interface that distinguish the PDP-11 port from neighboring GCC target modules.
